answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity. Every agent must lock a stake before it can grade answers or claim rewards, and peers can challenge any identity whose behavior looks coordinated. If a challenge proves a duplicate, the stake is slashed and the rewards are clawed back. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents has to lock a thousand bonds, so each Sybil costs real capital, and a single bad batch gets caught and burned before it can drift like timber on a gale. When honest stake outweighs the fakes, the tide of verified agents keeps the network anchored.
